record.original_question: Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be written as quotients S / p = {x in N | px in S} of numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 3 by a positive integer, and determine whether every numerical semigroup arises in this way.

evidence.quote: The next step in this line of research would be studying those numerical semigroups that are the quotient of a numerical semigroup with embedding dimension three by a positive integer. Unfortunately we do not have a procedure that allows us to distinguish such a semigroup from the rest. Moreover, we still do not know of any example of semigroups that are not of this form.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. The embedding dimension of $S$ is the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators. Given a numerical semigroup $S$ and a positive integer $p$, the quotient of $S$ by $p$ is defined as
$$\frac{S}{p} = \{x \in \mathbb{N} : px \in S\},$$
which is itself a numerical semigroup.

(a) Give an algorithmic characterization of those numerical semigroups $T$ that can be expressed in the form $T = S/p$ for some numerical semigroup $S$ of embedding dimension $3$ and some positive integer $p$.

(b) Decide whether every numerical semigroup arises in this way, that is, whether for each numerical semigroup $T$ there exist a numerical semigroup $S$ of embedding dimension $3$ and a positive integer $p$ such that $T = S/p$. If not, exhibit a numerical semigroup that cannot be so expressed.
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) has been resolved negatively: explicit families of numerical semigroups that are not quotients of any embedding-dimension-3 numerical semigroup have been constructed (e.g., families with generators of the form 2a+2^i, i=0,1,2,3, giving the first known examples of semigroups that are not 3-quotients). However, the characterization problem in part (a) — providing an algorithmic procedure to decide whether a given numerical semigroup is such a quotient — appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The multiples of a numerical semigroup
status_evidence.snippet: Recently, in [2, Theorem 3.1], examples of numerical semigroups that have no multiples of embedding dimension k are given for (fixed) k≥3. Today it is still an open problem to give an algorithmic procedure that determines whether a given numerical semigroup has a multiple with embedding dimension greater than or equal to three.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of numerical semigroups not arising as quotients of embedding-dimension-3 semigroups exist, but the algorithmic characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: When is a numerical semigroup a quotient?
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 3.1 constructs a family of numerical semigroups with embedding dimension k+1 that cannot be written as k-quotients; for k=3 this yields the first known examples of numerical semigroups that are not 3-quotients.
status_evidence.claim: Concrete families of numerical semigroups that are not quotients of embedding-dimension-3 semigroups have been exhibited.
